official.deadline_note: The 11th edition (academic year 2026-2027) closed on 11 May 2026 at 18:00 Italian time. The programme site announces 'IL NUOVO BANDO APRE NEL 2027!' / 'NEW APPLICATION OPENS 2027!', so the 12th edition opens in 2027 but no opening or closing date has been published.
official.application_cycle: 2026-2027 academic year (11th edition); 12th edition announced for 2027
official.status_note: The official programme site displays the banner 'IL NUOVO BANDO APRE NEL 2027!' / 'NEW APPLICATION OPENS 2027!', announcing that the new call opens in 2027. The 11th edition (2026-2027) received 1634 applications, 982 were eligible and 211 scholarships were awarded.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Winners are 'exempt from paying enrolment fees and university contributions', with the sole exception of the regional tax for the Right to Education, stamp duty, and any costs relating to accident and/or civil liability insurance and health insurance (Article 9 of the Call).
official.funding_period: per academic year (9 months of study), paid quarterly
benefits: Annual scholarship of EUR 10,800 paid quarterly into an Italian bank account held in the holder's name: EUR 4,800 for the October-December 2026 quarter, EUR 3,000 for January-March 2027 and EUR 3,000 for April-June 2027

Exemption from enrolment fees and university contributions at the participating institution, except regional tax for the Right to Education, stamp duty, accident and/or civil liability insurance and health insurance
Compulsory internship of at least 480 hours (three months) in an Italian company or professional association representative of the region
Study of Italian language and culture integrated into the programme, including a mandatory attendance verification
Compulsory seminar or training module on gender equality and the prevention of violence against women, in memory of Giulia Cecchettin
Tax exemption under Article 3, paragraph 3, letter d-ter of the Consolidated Income Tax Law for IRPEF purposes

Borse Ateneo scholarships offered by six participating universities: Università di Parma, Università degli Studi di Firenze, Università degli Studi di Bergamo, Università degli Studi della Tuscia, Università Ca' Foscari Venezia, Università degli Studi di Brescia
A reserved quota of Design Scholarships for Architecture and Design courses for applicants from India, Indonesia, Türkiye, Brazil and Ethiopia
eligibility: Citizens of Argentina, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Egypt, Ethiopia, Ghana, India, Indonesia, Iran, Kazakhstan, Mexico, Mongolia, Paraguay, Peru, People's Republic of China, Tunisia, Türkiye, Uruguay or Vietnam, permanently resident in that country
Hold an academic qualification valid for enrolment in a Master's/Postgraduate degree programme at the chosen institution; students who are about to graduate are not eligible

Have submitted an application for pre-admission to a course included in the IYT programme, following each university's own procedures; no exceptions are made for courses or universities not in the Project
May apply for only one course, with a second binding preference permitted for limited-enrolment (numero chiuso) courses
Born on or after 1 January 2000, except applicants for scholarship renewal
Certification of English language proficiency from level B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference
Certification of knowledge of Italian issued by the institution where training was undertaken, or a declaration of commitment to attend a classroom or self-study Italian course before departure
Not currently studying at an Italian university and not holding an Italian university degree
Both academic studies and the scholarship must start in October; deferral to the second semester is not possible
requirements: Applications must be submitted exclusively online through the programme's My-App registration page
Online applications for the 11th edition were submitted between 20 April 2026 and 11 May 2026 at 18:00 Italian time
Names and surnames must be entered exactly as they appear on the passport machine-readable zone
Multiple applications using different email addresses are strictly prohibited and will be rejected
Documents must be in English, French or Spanish, or translated by an official translator with both original and translation submitted
All files must be in PDF format (only the video in MP4), each document less than 1 MB and the video less than 10 MB; recommended browsers are Mozilla Firefox and Microsoft Edge
Incomplete applications are not considered eligible and documents cannot be sent by email; a submitted application cannot be edited
The scholarship only covers attendance at courses in Italy: university international mobility programmes, company internships abroad and thesis research abroad are not possible
The award of the scholarship is subject to prior review of legality by the Court of Auditors, so the actual award depends on the positive outcome of those checks
Courses are published on the basis of a written undertaking by the relevant Rector, subject to withdrawal within 60 days if the University's governing bodies do not ratify participation
documents: Certificate of completed exams (final transcript) for the qualification valid for enrolment in the Master's/University Master's programme, including the degree mark/CGPA; if the degree is complete but the certificate not yet issued, a certificate or statement from the university on headed paper, dated and signed by an official of the secretary's office

Certification of English language proficiency from level B2 CEFR (Cambridge, IELTS, TOEFL iBT, ISE Digital or ISE Paper - Trinity College, PTE, Linguaskill, ESOL, TOEIC covering listening, reading, speaking and writing); an English-taught degree certificate may be accepted as proof of level C1; the Duolingo certificate is not accepted

Certification of knowledge of the Italian language issued by the institution where training was undertaken, or a declaration of commitment to attend a classroom or self-study Italian course before departure

A video of no longer than 59 seconds explaining the reasons for wanting to study in Italy, professional goals and how the candidate would benefit from an internship in an Italian company; it may be filmed in English or Italian, with Italian viewed positively in evaluation
A Curriculum vitae et studiorum, maximum one page
A valid passport; citizens with dual nationality (Italian and foreign) must upload both passports; I.R.E. (Italian Resident Abroad) status gives rise to no reservations
selection_criteria: Comparative evaluation of applications by the Technical Committee of the IYT Programme (MAECI, ICE and Uni-Italia), which may use an ad hoc Commission, against the requirements of Articles 3 and 5 of the Call
Scholarships are allocated in quotas defined for each country
The Design Scholarship quota is allocated through specially drawn-up rankings taking into account the order of preference for courses given by the applicant
The Borse Ateneo quota is likewise assigned through specially established rankings based on the stated order of preference among courses
coverage: Annual scholarship of EUR 10,800 paid quarterly into an Italian bank account held in the scholar's name
Exemption from enrolment fees and university contributions at the participating institution
Compulsory internship at an Italian company or professional association representative of the region
Seminar or training module on gender equality and the fight against gender-based violence in the academic curriculum
Study of Italian language and culture within the programme
Explicitly NOT covered: travel expenses, accommodation, regional tax for the Right to Education, stamp duty, accident and/or civil liability insurance and health insurance
application_method: Check the courses listed in the Invest Your Talent in Italy section and contact the chosen university for pre-admission, indicating that you are an IYT applicant
Register on the IYT portal (My-App) using full name and surname exactly as printed on the passport

Upload the required documents: final transcript with CGPA (or the dated and signed university statement if the certificate is pending), English proficiency certification from B2, Italian certification or commitment declaration, a video of no longer than 59 seconds, a one-page CV and a valid passport
Submit the application online during the published call window

Await the Technical Committee's comparative evaluation; successful candidates are informed by email to the registration address and must return a signed Scholarship Commitment Letter within three days
official.application_route: Submit a pre-admission application to the chosen IYT course directly with that university, then apply online exclusively through the IYT My-App portal.
official.citizenship_residency: Citizens of the 23 listed partner countries who are permanently resident there
official.international_eligibility: Open to foreign students from the listed partner countries; students currently studying at or graduated from an Italian university are not eligible
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The course must be included in the IYT programme course list (Engineering-Advanced Technology, Management-Economics, Design-Architecture are the programme's areas of study); the reserved quota of Design Scholarships for Architecture and Design courses is limited to applicants from India, Indonesia, Türkiye, Brazil and Ethiopia
official.duration: 9 months of study, starting 1 October 2026 for the 2026-2027 academic year; renewable for the second year of a Master's course if conditions are met
official.description: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation - Directorate General for Growth and Export Promotion, the ICE Agency and Uni-Italia offer scholarships to foreign students to attend a Master's or Postgraduate course at a participating Italian university, completed with a compulsory internship at an Italian company or professional association. The programme aims to promote the internationalization of the Italian academic system and to strengthen collaboration between universities and businesses, and it is dedicated to the memory of Giulia Cecchettin.
official.english_requirement: Certification of English language proficiency from level B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference is required, including Cambridge, IELTS, TOEFL iBT, ISE Digital or ISE Paper - Trinity College, PTE, Linguaskill, ESOL and TOEIC covering listening, reading, speaking and writing. Candidates who obtained a university degree at the end of a course taught in English may submit a university certificate attesting English as the language of instruction, accepted as proof of level C1. The Duolingo certificate is not accepted. Courses are taught entirely in English. A separate requirement applies to Italian: certification issued by the institution where training was undertaken, or a declaration of commitment to attend a course before departure; Italian certification is not mandatory but contributes to the evaluation score.

not_confirmed: Whether the EUR 10,800 covers living costs, as the official pages state only the amount and the payment schedule without describing it as a living-cost allowance
The exact opening and closing dates of the 12th edition, which the official site announces only as opening in 2027
The scholarship amount and eligibility rules of the 12th edition, since they have not yet been published
verification.notes: Amount (EUR 10,800), quarterly payment schedule, tuition/fee exemption, exclusions from coverage, eligibility rules, required documents, English-language requirement, application procedure and the status of the current round were all read directly from the MAECI/ICE/Uni-Italia call, how-it-works and FAQ pages on the esteri.it domain, and the 2027 banner was read on the programme's institutional site.

applicant_utility.summary: This scholarship pays EUR 10,800 across nine months in Italy with a guaranteed internship placement at an Italian company, and it waives your enrolment fees and university contributions at a participating institution. You still have to fund flights, accommodation, health insurance, the regional right-to-education tax and stamp duty yourself, so treat the EUR 10,800 as roughly EUR 1,200 a month for living while covering those extras from your own pocket. The 11th edition has closed and the programme has announced that the new call opens in 2027, so the practical move now is to line up your documents and your university pre-admission so you can submit within the historically short three-to-four week window.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent graduates aged 26 or under from the 23 partner countries who want an English-taught Italian Master's plus a real internship placement and are comfortable with Italy as a base rather than a scholarship that pays for travel.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure pre-admission to an IYT-listed course at a participating university first; the scholarship is void if your course is not on the programme's list
Book an accepted English test early (B2 minimum) and avoid Duolingo, which the programme explicitly rejects
If your degree was taught in English, request the medium-of-instruction certificate well in advance, since registrars are slow and it is your only route to C1 recognition
Prepare a final transcript with CGPA, or a signed letterhead statement from the registrar if your diploma is still pending
Film the 59-second video in Italian rather than English, since the FAQ states the choice of Italian is considered positively
Compress every document to under 1 MB in PDF and the video to under 10 MB in MP4 before the portal closes at 18:00 Italian time
Have your passport machine-readable zone to hand so your name is entered character-for-character as the portal requires
common_rejection_risks: Applying for a course that is not on the IYT list, or a second application under a different email address, both of which lead to outright rejection
Applying while still completing your bachelor's degree: students about to graduate are ineligible by rule
Already studying at or holding a degree from an Italian university, which disqualifies you outright
Being over the age cut-off of 1 January 2000 if you are not a renewal applicant
Submitting documents in a language other than English, French or Spanish without an official translation, or an incomplete file that cannot be topped up by email
Deferring enrolment to the second semester, which forfeits the scholarship
Choosing a non-IYT course or changing course after selection, which voids eligibility
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Flights to and from Italy, accommodation for the nine months, health insurance, accident and civil liability insurance, the regional tax for the Right to Education and stamp duty, plus the cost of any pre-departure Italian course you commit to.
document_audit: Your transcript and degree certificate must be in English, French or Spanish, and if not you need both the original and a certified translation scanned into one file
The video is a hard cap at 59 seconds and the CV at one page; over-length files are the most common self-inflicted loss of points
If your degree certificate is pending you need a dated, signed statement on university letterhead from the secretary's office, not a self-declaration

Renewal applicants need the CFU exam certificate, an Italian-course attendance certificate and an internship project uploaded by 20 July, plus 30 credits achieved and verified attendance to keep the fee exemption
alerts: The 12th edition is announced for 2027 with no published dates; the 11th edition window was only about three weeks (20 April to 11 May 2026), so do not expect a long runway
The award is subject to a positive Court of Auditors legality review, and course listings can be withdrawn within 60 days if a university fails to ratify participation
IYT cannot be combined with any other Italian government or public-institution scholarship, including Erasmus+ and regional education scholarships
All mobility is barred: no Erasmus exchange, no internship abroad and no thesis research abroad, and internship paperwork must be completed by 20 January 2027 for the 11th edition cohort
The first payment only lands after you have enrolled and produced enrolment and attendance certificates, so you need bridge funds for arrival, deposit and first weeks
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Two parallel tracks: a pre-admission request to your chosen university plus an online application on the IYT My-App portal, evaluated comparatively by the Technical Committee with results emailed in summer.

official.deadline_note: Applications for all fields other than Economics must be submitted online by 16 October 2026 at 14:00 CEST; after that date the form stays active for one further week only for applicants to the Department of Economics, until 1 March 2027 at 14:00 CET. Reference letters must also arrive by the same deadline and are not accepted late.
official.application_cycle: 2027-2028 fellowship year, starting 1 September 2027; application process open from mid-July 2026 to the 16 October 2026 deadline
official.status_note: The Max Weber Programme page states 'Applications now open for the MWP fellowships' with a programme start date of 1 September 2027 and an application deadline of 16 October 2026 14:00 CEST.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Max Weber Fellowship is a postdoctoral stipend rather than an enrolled degree, and the Conditions of Award publish no tuition waiver or tuition coverage wording.
benefits: Basic grant of 2,500 EUR per month

Household allowance of up to 310 EUR per month for Fellows with a partner living with them in the Florence area, subject to the partner's income being below 2,000 EUR per month, and a dependents allowance of 210 EUR per month for each dependent child living with the Fellow in Florence

Health insurance: Max Weber Fellows are covered under the EUI's medical plan (basic plan) provided by Cigna at the expense of the EUI, unless they continue under their own active policies with proof of coverage
Research expenses of 1,500 EUR per year for eligible research expenses such as conference attendance, plus up to 1,000 EUR for job-interview expenses for Fellows on the job market

Reimbursement of the incoming trip to Florence and the outgoing trip at the end of the fellowship, up to a maximum of 1,200 EUR for both trips, and reimbursement of VISA fees up to 250 EUR; taxi expenses and visa-related accommodation or travel are not refundable and no refund is possible without receipts, including boarding passes for air travel

For qualifying Fellows in the second year in the Departments of Economics and Political and Social Sciences, the possibility of a 12-month part-time assistant professor contract (level ASSPR6/3) with net remuneration of approximately 850 EUR in addition to the monthly grant
Access to the research facilities and library of the European University Institute at Badia Fiesolana, with a personal mission and research fund of 1,500 EUR
Training and support in publishing, presenting, teaching and applying for research grants and jobs, with attention to communicating effectively in English
Parental leave policy of up to four months paid parental leave, with the fellowship extended accordingly, and the possibility to defer the fellowship by a year for Fellows expecting a child
No provision for removal or installation expenses
eligibility: Candidates of any nationality are eligible

Candidates must have received their PhD within the past 5 years, or have official approval to defend their thesis by the programme start date of 1 September: for the 2027-28 call the PhD should have been received or submitted between 01/09/2022 and 01/09/2027, with the defence no later than 31/12/2027

Extensions to the five-year rule are allowed for applicants whose academic career was interrupted by maternity or paternity leave, illness or mandatory military service, cited in 'Additional Notes' with supporting documents
Preference is given to applicants who have only just completed their doctorate, have not had a postdoctoral fellowship before, and/or are on the job market

Early-stage researchers who are at the EUI at the time of the application deadline are not eligible, including those enrolled in the EUI Doctoral Programme or employed or on a fellowship hosted by the EUI; former EUI members must have been continuously away in a full-time occupation or fellowship for at least one year by the deadline
Candidates from the EUI's Widening countries are encouraged to apply and may be supported under the EUI Spreading Excellence Programme

Candidates with external funding must hold a scholarship from a recognised National or International Research Funding Council or Charity covering at least living and research costs equivalent to 15,000 EUR for 12 months (1,250 EUR per month), and health insurance valid in Italy for the whole fellowship
Applicants must fulfil the English language requirements, with an expected level of C1 of the Common European Framework of Reference
requirements: Doctoral thesis completed, or official approval to defend, within the five-year window

Research proposal for the postdoctoral project, maximum two pages as a PDF, with well-defined and realistic goals achievable within the fellowship duration, indicating plans for the first 12 and second 12 months for a 24-month application, and including a reflection on how gender and diversity are relevant to the proposed research
Academic career statement, one page as a PDF, setting out research and teaching interests and experience and career plans
CV with a list of publications in PDF
A copy of the passport as a JPEG

At least two and at most three academic referees, with at least two letters of reference submitted online directly by the referees by the deadline; references from current full-time or part-time EUI professors are not accepted
Documents must use standard international fonts without macros, special characters or password protection

Academic career statement and research proposal must meet the requirements of the EUI Guidelines for the Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence for Research, including acknowledgement and reference of any AI-generated content
documents: CV with a list of publications (PDF)
Research proposal, 2 pages (PDF), including the required reflection on gender and diversity

At least two letters of reference submitted online by the referees by the deadline (dossier services such as Interfolio are accepted if the original letters arrive by the deadline and are not disclosed to the applicant)
For applicants with external funding: proof of funding, and for internal candidates a supporting letter by the EUI mentor and by the EUI Head of department of affiliation
selection_criteria: Academic accomplishments and potential: the candidate's contributions such as publications and PhD thesis, commitment to an academic career as outlined in the academic career statement, and supporting evidence including two letters of reference, with preference for applicants entering straight after their doctorate or in the early stages of their post-doctoral career
Research proposal: a clear and well-structured proposal with achievable goals during the fellowship
Mentorship: capacity and availability of the EUI faculty for mentoring the candidate, with common research interests helpful but not required

Additional consideration is given to country of origin and doctoral studies, gender and the candidate's background, and diversity in terms of gender and background as well as synergies between academic units are considered
coverage: Basic grant of 2,500 EUR per month
Health insurance under the EUI medical plan at the expense of the EUI
Mission and research fund of 1,500 EUR per year, plus up to 1,000 EUR for job-interview expenses for Fellows on the job market
Reimbursement of incoming and outgoing travel to a maximum of 1,200 EUR and VISA fees to a maximum of 250 EUR
Household allowance of up to 310 EUR per month and dependents allowance of 210 EUR per month per dependent child, where applicable
No provision for removal or installation expenses
application_method: Register the online application as early as possible on the EUI OSIRIS portal (apply.eui.eu), process code MWP-APPLY, entering personal details and referee details so that referees can submit reference letters before the deadline

Continue working on the application details and attachments until the deadline of 16 October 2026 at 14:00 CEST, submitting only once all information is filled in correctly and the final documents uploaded
Academic units may choose to interview some candidates online
Applicants wishing to be considered for the EUI-IHEID Fellowship, the Alcide De Gasperi Research Centre affiliation, or external-funding schemes indicate this in the application form
official.application_route: Apply online through the EUI OSIRIS application portal (process MWP-APPLY), registering referee details early because references must arrive by the same deadline.
official.study_mode: Full-time, residential; fellows must live in the area of Florence for the duration of the fellowship
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality restriction; candidates of any nationality are eligible
official.international_eligibility: Open to applicants from anywhere in the world regardless of nationality; the EUI assists non-EU fellows with visa and residence requirements, including family members
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: For the historical, humanities and social sciences, with affiliation to one of the EUI's academic units: Department of Economics, Department of History, Department of Law, Department of Political and Social Sciences, Robert Schuman Centre for Advanced Studies or Florence School of Transnational Governance. Additional grants funded by governments or foundations in Finland, Germany, Greece, Poland and Japan are available to nationals and in some cases residents of those countries, and a suitable applicant of any nationality may be considered for an additional year at the IHEID in Geneva.
official.research_requirement: A research proposal of two pages is required, with well-defined and realistic goals achievable within the duration of the fellowship, plans for the first and second 12 months for a 24-month application, and a reflection on how gender and diversity are relevant to the proposed research.
official.duration: 12 months for the Department of Law; 12 or 24 months for Economics, History, Political and Social Sciences and the Robert Schuman Centre; 24 months for the Florence School of Transnational Governance; all fellowships run from September to August and only in exceptional cases can support be extended to 36 months
official.description: The Max Weber Programme is the postdoctoral programme of the European University Institute, a unique programme in the historical, humanities and social sciences, open to applicants within five years of completing their PhD from anywhere in the world regardless of nationality. It is highly selective with an annual acceptance rate of under 2%, and a cohort typically consists of around 65 Fellows across the EUI's academic units.
official.english_requirement: The expected level of English proficiency is level C1 of the Common European Framework of Reference. An English certificate is not requested as part of the application, but successful candidates must provide a certificate or supporting document on registration: IELTS from 7.5, TOEFL (IBT) from 110, Cambridge Proficiency A/B/C or Cambridge English: Advanced (CAE) A/B; alternatively a document showing that the candidate has written the doctorate, published an article or book chapter of at least 6,000 words in English, or pursued postgraduate studies in an English-language degree programme. Native English speakers are exempt from proof, and an expired certificate is accepted if it expired no more than three years ago. The official working language of the programme is English, and documents submitted in English guarantee the widest possible reading.

not_confirmed: Tuition coverage, since the Conditions of Award are silent on tuition for a postdoctoral fellowship and publish no waiver wording
verification.notes: Deadline of 16 October 2026 at 14:00 CEST, start date of 1 September 2027, grant of 2,500 EUR per month, family allowances, Cigna health insurance, 1,500 EUR research fund, travel and visa reimbursement caps, request documents, C1 English level with the recognised test scores, selection criteria and the under-2% acceptance rate were all read directly from the EUI's own apply pages and the Max Weber Programme site.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a residential postdoctoral fellowship at Badia Fiesolana near Florence paying 2,500 EUR a month for 12 or 24 months, with EUI-paid health insurance, 1,500 EUR a year for research and job-market costs, up to 1,200 EUR of travel and 250 EUR of visa fees reimbursed, and family allowances if you have a partner or children living with you. The deadline of 16 October 2026 at 14:00 CEST is also the deadline for your reference letters, so your referees must be registered in the portal weeks before then. Budget for relocation yourself because there is no installation allowance, and note that August carries no grant and that you must live in the Florence area throughout.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career researchers in history, law, economics, political and social sciences or transnational governance who finished their doctorate within the last five years, have a concrete research project and want a year or two of protected writing time with EUI mentorship.
application_readiness_checklist: Register referee details in the OSIRIS portal weeks ahead of 16 October, because referees are only emailed after you complete that first step and late letters cannot be accepted

Identify two full-time EUI professors whose research genuinely matches your project, since mentorship capacity is an explicit selection criterion and references from current EUI professors are rejected
Draft the two-page proposal as a plan the committee can believe you can deliver inside the fellowship window, with explicit 12-month and 24-month milestones if you request two years
Write the mandatory gender-and-diversity reflection into the proposal rather than bolting it on, since the form asks for it directly
Keep every PDF free of macros, special characters and password protection, and upload the passport as a JPEG
Check that your PhD defence is scheduled no later than 31 December 2027 if you are submitting before you defend
Do not contact EUI faculty for individual proposal guidance, since the EUI explicitly declines it and it will not help your file
common_rejection_risks: With an acceptance rate under 2% and only around 40 of roughly 65 cohort places filled each year, the strongest risk is a proposal that reads as too large to finish or poorly matched to available mentors
Reference letters arriving after 14:00 CEST on 16 October, which the EUI says will not be accepted and which can leave your dossier incomplete at the moment selection begins
Being currently enrolled, employed or on fellowship at the EUI at the deadline, or having left the EUI less than a full-time year before it
Applying to the Florence School of Transnational Governance without intending the full two years, since it only offers 24-month fellowships
A proposal that ignores the gender-and-diversity reflection the form explicitly requests
Using generative AI to write substantive parts of the statement or proposal without acknowledgement, contrary to the EUI guidelines the form cites
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Removal and installation to Florence are explicitly not provided, August is unpaid, and taxis plus visa-related accommodation and travel are non-refundable; family travel is reimbursed only for the Fellow, not dependants.
document_audit: The proposal is capped at two pages, though bibliography and references may slightly exceed the cap; the career statement is capped at one page
You must supply a minimum of two and a maximum of three referees, so choosing three gives you no margin if one never submits
Interfolio or dossier-service letters are acceptable only if the original arrives by the deadline and is not disclosed to you
Externally funded applicants must document a scholarship covering at least 15,000 EUR for 12 months and Italian health insurance, and face a separate 1 February to 31 March call
If your English certificate has expired you can still use it provided it lapsed no more than three years ago
alerts: The Guardian-style trap is the reference deadline: applications for non-Economics fields close hard at 14:00 CEST on 16 October 2026, while Economics applicants get until 1 March 2027, so a late referee is fatal
If you already receive a grant or salary you must disclose it and the fellowship is cut to a minimum of 1,750 EUR per month depending on the additional income
Arriving after the start of September, leaving before 20 July or being absent for the month of August reduces or terminates the grant
Eligibility uses the submission date too: your PhD must be received or submitted between 1 September 2022 and 1 September 2027, and defended by 31 December 2027

Special grants from Finland, Germany, Greece, Poland, Japan, the IHEID Geneva place, Canon, Kohli and the CIVICA postdoctoral exchange vary from year to year and eligible applicants are considered automatically, so check the Information for Applicants tab rather than assuming
Fellows with a child during the fellowship can take up to four months of paid parental leave with the fellowship extended, and may defer the start by a year
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on OSIRIS with process MWP-APPLY, add referees immediately so their letters arrive by the deadline, upload CV, career statement, proposal and passport, then academic units rank candidates and the Fellowship Steering Committee decides, with results by the end of January (end of March for Economics).
